item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: An international team of astronomers using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has discovered a brand-new class of cosmic object — a black hole star — located billions of light-years away in the constellation Cetus, radiating 100 billion times more energy than any known star.

item.dc:creator: Daily Science News

item.title: One of Britain's Finest Jurassic Fossil Collections Sold to Abu Dhabi Natural History Museum
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: A rare and historically significant fossil collection from the UK's Jurassic Coast, comprising 318 specimens including new species, has been sold to the Natural History Museum in Abu Dhabi after British institutions failed to secure funding, sparking national debate over heritage preservation.

media:content.media:title: One of Britain's Finest Jurassic Fossil Collections Sold to Abu Dhabi Natural History Museum

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Used to Create a Virus for the First Time in Stanford University Breakthrough
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: Scientists at Stanford University have for the first time successfully designed and produced a new bacteriophage virus using AI models Evo1 and Evo2, marking a major medical breakthrough while raising urgent global biosafety concerns.

media:content.media:title: Artificial Intelligence Used to Create a Virus for the First Time in Stanford University Breakthrough

item.title: World's Most Powerful Solar Telescope Releases Clearest-Ever Images of the Sun's Surface
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: The Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope in Hawaii has released the highest-resolution images ever obtained of the Sun's photosphere, capturing for the first time tiny Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities just 20 km wide — potentially solving the century-old mystery of why the Sun's corona is millions of degrees hotter than its surface.

media:content.media:title: World's Most Powerful Solar Telescope Releases Clearest-Ever Images of the Sun's Surface

item.title: More Than Half the World's Reservoirs Face Inactivation by 2060 Due to Sedimentation Crisis
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: A major study reveals over half of the world's 550,000+ reservoirs face partial or complete inactivation by 2060 due to sediment accumulation, threatening water supply for more than 2 billion people and putting 26% of globally irrigated farmland at severe risk of water scarcity.

media:content.media:title: More Than Half the World's Reservoirs Face Inactivation by 2060 Due to Sedimentation Crisis

item.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 Upper Stage Crashes Into the Moon — Creating a 27-Meter Crater
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket upper stage, launched in January 2025 and abandoned in a high Earth orbit after its fuel ran out, crashed into the lunar surface on August 5, 2026, creating a crater approximately 27 meters wide — providing scientists with valuable data about space debris risks to future Moon missions.

media:content.media:title: SpaceX Falcon 9 Upper Stage Crashes Into the Moon — Creating a 27-Meter Crater

item.title: Dinosaur-Killing Asteroid Impact Released Heat 17 Times Greater Than Maximum Human Tolerance, New Study Reveals
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: A new study reveals the 66-million-year-old Chicxulub asteroid impact generated heat 17 times beyond human tolerance limits, instantly killing open-air dinosaurs within hours and triggering massive global wildfires — overturning the previous 'impact winter' theory of dinosaur extinction.

media:content.media:title: Dinosaur-Killing Asteroid Impact Released Heat 17 Times Greater Than Maximum Human Tolerance, New Study Reveals

item.title: Volcanic Eruptions in the Pacific Ring of Fire Have Been Cooling the Earth for Centuries
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: A new study from the University of Basel reveals that volcanic eruptions in the Pacific Ring of Fire caused over 22 mysterious long-term cooling periods across the past 12,000 years, with more than 80% of glacier expansion events coinciding with major volcanic events.

media:content.media:title: Volcanic Eruptions in the Pacific Ring of Fire Have Been Cooling the Earth for Centuries

item.title: Africa's First Lunar Mission to Be Carried to the Moon by China in 2029
item.dc:creator: Daily Science News
item.description: Africa's first space exploration mission — known as BALLS (Bounced African Low Lunar Sphere) — is scheduled to be launched to the Moon's south pole in 2029 aboard China's Chang'e-8 lunar vehicle, marking a historic milestone for African space science.

media:content.media:title: Africa's First Lunar Mission to Be Carried to the Moon by China in 2029

item.title: The Future of Jodrell Bank Observatory at Risk
item.dc:creator: BBC News
item.description: The iconic Jodrell Bank Observatory in the UK faces closure by April 2028 due to funding cuts, threatening 28 jobs and affecting 3,000 scientists. The UNESCO World Heritage site's £2.8 million annual budget is being redirected by UKRI.

media:content.media:title: The Future of Jodrell Bank Observatory at Risk

item.dc:creator: Purdue University / Archaeological Legacy Institute
item.description: Scientists prepare a new expedition to Nikumaroro Island after satellite photos reveal the 'Taraia Object' — a shape matching Amelia Earhart's Lockheed Electra — potentially solving aviation's greatest mystery after 89 years.

media:content.media:title: Clue Found on Nikumaroro Island Regarding Earhart's Disappearance

item.title: What Are the Mysterious 'Little Red Dots' from the Early Universe?
item.dc:creator: University of Texas at Austin
item.description: New research from the University of Texas suggests the mysterious 'Little Red Dots' observed by the James Webb Space Telescope have evolved into today's star clusters, solving a cosmic puzzle about the early universe.

media:content.media:title: What Are the Mysterious 'Little Red Dots' from the Early Universe?

item.title: Orcas Observed Ramming Sunfish into Pieces
item.dc:creator: Frontiers in Ethology
item.description: Scientists uncover remarkable behavior of killer whales in the Gulf of California, where orcas ram giant sunfish at high speed to break their tough collagen-rich skin into manageable pieces.

media:content.media:title: Orcas Observed Ramming Sunfish into Pieces

item.title: Wreckage of Pan Am Aircraft Discovered on Ocean Floor After 74 Years
item.dc:creator: Deep Sea Vision / Discovery Channel
item.description: Explorers discover the wreckage of Pan Am's 'Clipper Endeavor' on the ocean floor at 2,000 feet depth, 74 years after its 1952 crash off Puerto Rico that killed 52 people and led to modern airline safety briefings.

media:content.media:title: Wreckage of Pan Am Aircraft Discovered on Ocean Floor After 74 Years

item.title: Double Star System Where Both Stars Exploded as Supernovae Discovered for the First Time
item.dc:creator: Stanford University / Nature Communications
item.description: Scientists discover the first known binary star system where both stars exploded as supernovae, using 16 years of Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope data to identify the twin remnants in the Jellyfish Nebula region.

media:content.media:title: Double Star System Where Both Stars Exploded as Supernovae Discovered for the First Time

item.title: India Becomes the Third Country in the World to Successfully Test a Private-Sector Orbital Rocket
item.dc:creator: Science News Hub
item.description: Indian company Skyroot Aerospace successfully launched its first private orbital rocket Vikram-1 from Sriharikota, making India the third country after the US and China with private-sector orbital launch capability.

media:content.media:title: India Becomes the Third Country in the World to Successfully Test a Private-Sector Orbital Rocket

item.title: A New Conservation Measure to Save Koalas from Extinction
item.dc:creator: Science News Hub
item.description: University of Queensland researchers have launched a project to cryopreserve koala eggs and sperm in liquid nitrogen at -196°C, creating a genetic backup to prevent the complete extinction of koalas.

media:content.media:title: A New Conservation Measure to Save Koalas from Extinction

item.title: First Medical X-Ray Images Taken in Space
item.dc:creator: Science News Hub
item.description: Astronauts on the private Fram2 Crew Dragon mission have successfully taken the first medical X-ray images in space, confirming a compact new X-ray device can identify health problems on future Moon and Mars journeys.

media:content.media:title: First Medical X-Ray Images Taken in Space

item.title: US Space Force Acquires New Electromagnetic Weapon Capable of Disabling Satellites
item.dc:creator: Science News Hub
item.description: The U.S. Space Force has acquired its first offensive electromagnetic weapon system, 'Meadowlands,' capable of emitting streams of electromagnetic radiation to disrupt enemy satellite signals without causing physical damage.

media:content.media:title: US Space Force Acquires New Electromagnetic Weapon Capable of Disabling Satellites

item.title: A Previously Undiscovered 'Mystery' Substance Found on Pluto and Titan
item.dc:creator: James Webb Space Telescope Research Team
item.description: The James Webb Space Telescope has detected evidence of a brand new, unidentified chemical substance on both Pluto and Titan. The mysterious molecule absorbs a specific wavelength of light and has never been found anywhere else in the solar system.

media:content.media:title: A Previously Undiscovered 'Mystery' Substance Found on Pluto and Titan

item.title: World's First Nuclear-Powered Commercial Satellite Successfully Launched into Space
item.dc:creator: SpaceX & City Labs
item.description: SpaceX launched the first commercial nuclear-powered satellite, BOHR, under the Transporter-17 mission. Developed by City Labs, the CubeSat uses a NanoTritium nuclear battery, enabling continuous power in deep space where solar panels are ineffective.

media:content.media:title: World's First Nuclear-Powered Commercial Satellite Successfully Launched into Space

item.title: A New Scientific Explanation for Fermi's Paradox
item.dc:creator: Sergiy Ivliev & Astrophysicist Sergei Popov
item.description: New research suggests advanced extraterrestrial civilizations may have handed over space exploration to superintelligent AI, choosing silent, efficient existence over noisy empire-building. This could explain why we see no signs of alien life despite the universe's vastness.

media:content.media:title: A New Scientific Explanation for Fermi's Paradox

item.title: A New Earth-Like Planet Potentially Suitable for Life Discovered Near Our Solar System
item.dc:creator: University of California, McDonald Observatory & Kitt Peak National Observatory
item.description: Astronomers have discovered GJ 3378b, an Earth-like planet 25 light-years away orbiting a red dwarf star within the habitable zone. Twice the size of Earth, this cosmic neighbor is a promising candidate for future life-searching research.

media:content.media:title: A New Earth-Like Planet Potentially Suitable for Life Discovered Near Our Solar System

item.title: The World's Most Powerful Particle Accelerator Shut Down Until 2030 for Upgrades
item.dc:creator: CERN Research Organization
item.description: The Large Hadron Collider at CERN has been shut down for a four-year upgrade program (LS3) to become the High-Luminosity LHC. With ten times the sensitivity and triple the collision rate, scientists hope to open new frontiers in particle physics.

media:content.media:title: The World's Most Powerful Particle Accelerator Shut Down Until 2030 for Upgrades

item.title: The First Dinosaur Fossil from Antarctica, Hidden in a Drawer for Four Decades
item.dc:creator: British Antarctic Survey & Natural History Museum
item.description: A fossil forgotten in a drawer at the British Antarctic Survey for nearly forty years has been confirmed as the first dinosaur bone discovered from Antarctica — a tail vertebra from a titanosaur that lived 82 million years ago when the continent was covered in warm forests.

media:content.media:title: The First Dinosaur Fossil from Antarctica, Hidden in a Drawer for Four Decades

item.title: Swift Telescope Rescue Mission Today
item.dc:creator: NASA & Katalyst Space Technologies
item.description: NASA launches a historic mission to save the Swift space telescope from re-entering Earth's atmosphere. The robotic spacecraft LINK, aboard a Pegasus XL rocket, will attempt the first-ever commercial robotic capture and reboost of an aging satellite.

media:content.media:title: Swift Telescope Rescue Mission Today

item.title: 31 New Marine Species Discovered in the Ocean Off Brazil
item.dc:creator: Schmidt Ocean Institute Research Team
item.description: Scientists have discovered 31 new marine species in just two weeks during an expedition in international waters off Brazil. The finds include jellyfish, siphonophores, comb jellies, and giant single-celled organisms from the ocean's mysterious midwater zone.

media:content.media:title: 31 New Marine Species Discovered in the Ocean Off Brazil

item.title: The Heart of the Milky Way Seen Through the Euclid Space Telescope
item.dc:creator: European Space Agency (ESA) Euclid Team
item.description: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has released the largest and clearest image ever captured of the center of the Milky Way, containing over 60 million stars. This visible-light mosaic could open a new era in exoplanet discovery.

media:content.media:title: The Heart of the Milky Way Seen Through the Euclid Space Telescope

item.title: Environmental Experts Oppose Plan to Crash the International Space Station into the Ocean
item.dc:creator: Environmental Research & Policy Team
item.description: Environmental experts warn that NASA's plan to deliberately crash the 400-ton International Space Station into the ocean at Point Nemo could pose severe long-term threats to marine ecosystems, with toxic chemicals, batteries, and metal debris settling on the ocean floor.

media:content.media:title: Environmental Experts Oppose Plan to Crash the International Space Station into the Ocean

item.title: Modern Digital Technology Lends a Hand in Saving the Critically Endangered Vaquita
item.dc:creator: Florida Atlantic University Research Team
item.description: Scientists have digitally reconstructed the skeletal system of the vaquita porpoise using 3D technology. With only 7-10 individuals left in the wild, this digital preservation aims to support conservation and research efforts for the world's most endangered marine mammal.

media:content.media:title: Modern Digital Technology Lends a Hand in Saving the Critically Endangered Vaquita

item.title: New Supernova Remnant Discovered Near the Center of the Milky Way
item.dc:creator: Chandra & XMM-Newton Research Team
item.description: A team of astronomers has discovered a new supernova remnant located near the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way. Using data from Chandra and XMM-Newton, the remnant was found in the Sgr C region, approximately 26,000 light-years from Earth.

media:content.media:title: New Supernova Remnant Discovered Near the Center of the Milky Way

item.title: New Air Force One Enters Service
item.dc:creator: Science News Correspondent
item.description: US President Donald Trump attended the official unveiling ceremony of the new Air Force One — a luxurious Boeing 747-8i gifted to the United States from Qatar, valued at approximately $400 million.

media:content.media:title: New Air Force One Enters Service

item.title: The World's Black Box Being Built in Tasmania
item.dc:creator: Science News Correspondent
item.description: The 'Earth's Black Box' project — proposed to be built on the island of Tasmania to store data about Earth's climate change for future generations — has been restarted and is set to be installed by December 2026.

media:content.media:title: The World's Black Box Being Built in Tasmania

item.title: New Details Captured from a Radiation Jet of the M87 Black Hole
item.dc:creator: NASA Space Telescope Research Team
item.description: NASA X-ray space telescope reveals the most detailed X-ray data ever collected from M87's powerful radiation jet, showing unprecedented details about superluminal motion and jet dynamics spanning over a decade of observations.

media:content.media:title: New Details Captured from a Radiation Jet of the M87 Black Hole

item.title: Exoplanet WASP-121b: Where Rubies and Sapphires Rain Down
item.dc:creator: James Webb Space Telescope Research Team
item.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, researchers discover an ultra-hot Jupiter where rubies and sapphires rain from the sky. WASP-121b experiences extreme temperature differences, iron and gemstone rain, and winds exceeding 11,000 miles per hour.

media:content.media:title: Exoplanet WASP-121b: Where Rubies and Sapphires Rain Down

item.title: Global Underground Fungal Network Map Revealed
item.dc:creator: Science
item.description: A new global map reveals the vast scale of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks — vital underground systems that store carbon, support plants, and are threatened by modern agriculture.

media:content.media:title: Global Underground Fungal Network Map Revealed

item.title: Artemis III Astronauts Named
item.dc:creator: NASA
item.description: NASA announced a four-member crew for Artemis III — a high-risk 2027 crewed demonstration mission in Low Earth Orbit that will validate docking and landing procedures for future lunar landings.

media:content.media:title: Artemis III Astronauts Named

item.title: MAVEN Mars Spacecraft Makes Its Final Journey
item.dc:creator: NASA
item.description: After approximately six months of silence, NASA has officially confirmed that the MAVEN spacecraft orbiting Mars has gone completely offline, marking the end of a mission that carried out valuable observations of the Red Planet for over a decade.

media:content.media:title: MAVEN Mars Spacecraft Makes Its Final Journey

item.title: Scientists Make New Discovery About the Mysterious Sound Patterns of Humpback Whales
item.dc:creator: Alaska Whale Foundation
item.description: Scientists have for the first time identified that the mysterious deep sounds heard from coastal areas are being produced by humpback whales, revealing that whale communication abilities are far broader than previously thought.

media:content.media:title: Scientists Make New Discovery About the Mysterious Sound Patterns of Humpback Whales

item.title: British Paralympian John McFall Prepares to Become the First Disabled Astronaut to Orbit Earth
item.dc:creator: European Space Agency
item.description: British Paralympian and surgeon John McFall is on the verge of making history as the first person with a physical disability to live in space through a mission to Haven-1, the world's first proposed commercial space station.

media:content.media:title: British Paralympian John McFall Prepares to Become the First Disabled Astronaut to Orbit Earth

item.title: T. Rex's Tiny Arms — An Evolutionary Sacrifice for a Powerful Skull
item.dc:creator: University College London Research Team
item.description: A new study has solved the mystery of T. rex's disproportionately small arms, revealing they were the result of an evolutionary trade-off that allowed their skulls to evolve into a more powerful and larger form.

media:content.media:title: T. Rex's Tiny Arms — An Evolutionary Sacrifice for a Powerful Skull

item.title: Evidence Found That Red Dwarf Stars Are Swallowing Planets
item.dc:creator: Keele University & Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
item.description: Astronomers have discovered evidence that red dwarf stars are swallowing planets that orbit them, using data from the Gaia-ESO Spectroscopic Survey revealing unusually high levels of lithium in these stars' atmospheres.

media:content.media:title: Evidence Found That Red Dwarf Stars Are Swallowing Planets

item.title: Blue Origin's New Glenn Rocket Explodes During Pre-Launch Test
item.dc:creator: Blue Origin & NASA
item.description: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded in a massive fireball during a hotfire test at Cape Canaveral Space Center in Florida on May 28, 2026, threatening NASA's Artemis lunar mission timelines and a scheduled Amazon satellite deployment mission.

media:content.media:title: Blue Origin's New Glenn Rocket Explodes During Pre-Launch Test

item.title: Moon Base I Mission Awarded to Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin
item.dc:creator: NASA & Blue Origin
item.description: NASA officially selects Blue Origin for the first of three uncrewed lunar missions planned for 2026 as part of a $20 billion project to establish a lunar base, choosing the company over SpaceX to deliver equipment to the Moon's south pole.

media:content.media:title: Moon Base I Mission Awarded to Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin

item.title: Psyche Spacecraft Uses Mars Gravity Assist to Gain Speed
item.dc:creator: NASA

item.title: Amazing Paint Coating That Provides Water from Hot Air
item.dc:creator: Science & Technology Correspondent
item.description: A team of researchers from the University of Sydney has developed an advanced nanotechnology paint coating that can cool buildings while collecting water from the air through passive radiative cooling, offering a solution to heat and water scarcity worldwide.

media:content.media:title: Amazing Paint Coating That Provides Water from Hot Air

item.title: A Wasp Named in Honor of David Attenborough on His 100th Birthday
item.dc:creator: Natural History Correspondent
item.description: Scientists at the Natural History Museum in London have named a newly discovered genus of parasitic wasps after the world-renowned naturalist and broadcaster Sir David Attenborough on his 100th birthday.

media:content.media:title: A Wasp Named in Honor of David Attenborough on His 100th Birthday

item.title: A Tiny Object at the Edge of the Solar System Has an Atmosphere
item.dc:creator: Space Science Correspondent
item.description: Scientists have discovered that a mysterious atmosphere has formed around an extremely small celestial object located at the far edge of the solar system. The object, designated (612533) 2002 XV93, is a plutino in the Kuiper Belt.

media:content.media:title: A Tiny Object at the Edge of the Solar System Has an Atmosphere

item.title: Signing of Global Pandemic Treaty Delayed Once Again

item.dc:creator: Astronomy Correspondent
item.description: Astronomers reveal that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS originated from an extremely cold and isolated region of the Milky Way and may be the oldest interstellar object ever encountered at approximately 11 billion years old.

item.title: Scarlet Fever Existed in America Even Before Columbus's Arrival
item.dc:creator: Science & History Correspondent

item.title: Risk of Atlantic Ocean Current System Collapse on the Rise
item.dc:creator: Climate Research Correspondent
item.description: Latest scientific research reveals that the risk of collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is significantly higher than previously estimated, with new data putting the probability well above 50%.

media:content.media:title: Risk of Atlantic Ocean Current System Collapse on the Rise

item.title: Massive Mexican Government Data Theft Using Artificial Intelligence
item.dc:creator: Gambit Security
item.description: In what researchers describe as the world's largest cybersecurity breach, hackers used AI tools to steal hundreds of millions of sensitive records from Mexican government institutions over a 2.5-month period.

item.title: SpaceX Starlink Surpasses 10,000 Satellites in Low Earth Orbit — A Historic Milestone With Growing Concerns

item.description: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet constellation has crossed a remarkable threshold, surpassing 10,000 active satellites in low Earth orbit as of March 17, 2026.
